skill: Identify pivot columns of an already row-echelon-form integer matrix by locating the first nonzero entry in each nonzero row.
reasoning_steps: Scan each row left to right for its leading nonzero entry. Ignore all-zero rows.
Collect column indices containing these pivots.
Select exactly these columns in checkbox fields or the equivalent complete set in the radio bank. No elimination is required.
invariants: Input is already REF: increasing leading positions and zero rows at bottom.
Small integer matrices, observed shapes 3x3 through 5x5, preserve easy visual inspection workload.
Prompt asks pivot columns, not their count, nonpivot columns, or conversion to REF.
Complete checkbox bank has one field per column; observed radio source has five complete candidate subsets.
Solutions state leading-entry rule and identify actual columns.
permitted_variations: Change signed integer pivot values while keeping them nonzero.
Change entries to the right of pivots, including zero; this cannot affect the selected columns.

Change eligible increasing pivot-column assignments, rank within comparable workload, leading-zero columns, trailing nonpivot columns, and zero-row count. Source-specific labels, subset, correct-choice position and count are incidental, not requirements.
Vary matrix name and bank order independently of correctness.
For radio, derive alternative subsets from actual pivots and vary which mathematical set and answer position is correct.

response_contract.canonical_example: No answer fields captured; solution gives columns 2,3,4.

lesson_passages: The pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.
The pivot columns of a matrix in row echelon form are simply the columns in which the pivots appear.
scope_boundary: Later lesson step on general matrices explicitly requires conversion to REF; that operation belongs to later KPs, not this one.

source_cases.problem:
The row echelon form matrix $B$ is given below. What are its pivot columns?


$$
B=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$
source_cases.solution:
Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $B$ has $3$ pivots in the $2$nd, $3$rd, and $4$th columns:



$$
B=\begin{bmatrix}0 & \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{1} & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{-1} & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{1}\end{bmatrix}
$$
